---
title: "About Me"
---

I am an associate professor in the Department of Economics and faculty affiliate of the
Murphy Institute at Tulane University, as well as a Faculty Research Fellow at the
[NBER](https://www.nber.org/programs-projects/programs-working-groups/development-american-economy?page=1&perPage=50).
I received my Ph.D. in economics from the University of California, Irvine in 2019.

I am interested in how migration, racial violence, and other demographic shocks shape economic and political outcomes. My work lies at the intersection of applied microeconomics (especially topics in labor, urban, and public), political economy (focusing on American electoral politics), and economic history (focusing
on the U.S.). While at Tulane, I have taught courses at both the undergraduate and
graduate levels, including in microeconomic theory, political economy, and economic
history.

In my free time, I enjoy chatting about politics, writing fiction, making music, and spending time with my wife Amy and our two children (aged 3 and 5).
